subject: Escalation request: Avalon Therapeutics - research pilot clearance + pricing exception

Subject: Avalon Therapeutics - pilot request (need clearance + pricing exception)

Team — looping you in on a large strategic pilot with Avalon Therapeutics. Quick summary: they want a 6-week research pilot processing de-identified genomic variant data plus some metadata (no raw FASTQs). The ask: a capped pilot (up to 50M tokens) with a 30% pilot discount and a request for data to be processed in us-east-1 only.

Why this is sensitive: Avalon is a biotech with a German subcontractor for downstream analysis and operates in the EU/US; export/sanctions and data residency questions came up during procurement. They asked for a reduced legal appendix and one-off payment terms.

Attachments: Avalon_SOW_draft.pdf (SOW draft from customer)

Can deal desk/legal & security review for eligibility (export control / sanctions) and exec signoff for the pricing exception? They are requesting a signed SOW by 12/10 to hit their Q1 submission timeline.

Thanks — Lauren
Lauren Bishop

A few immediate requests from Deal Desk: 1) Please confirm the source of the genomic data (human subjects? de-identified?) and whether Avalon will be acting as controller/processor; 2) list of ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) for Avalon; 3) a short data flow diagram showing which systems/processors will touch the data (the German subcontractor is a flag).

Pricing exception: I can prepare an approval memo, but this must go to Rishi for exec signoff because the requested 30% pilot discount exceeds the standard pilot allowance and touches our revenue recognition concessions. We should include a proposed fallback (20% + credits tied to usage thresholds).

I'll open a Deal Desk case (DD-AV-3371) and add the SOW + any docs you send.

Thanks — marking this for exec review. A couple of comments:
- Security/compliance signoff (Vivek) required for export control / sanctions and to confirm whether the German subcontractor triggers an export control evaluation (technical data transfer to EU).
- Legal should weigh on the revised payment terms; if Avalon needs a single upfront invoice that will affect the SOW and AR terms.
- For pricing, I will consider approving a pilot discount up to 25% if the Deal Desk and Security can agree to the conditions (data residency hard restriction to us-east-1, contractual clause excluding certain sequence-level outputs, and KYC clearance). Anything above 25% needs documented strategic rationale (partner status, reference customer, or enterprise expansion opportunity).

Please consolidate the UBOs, the SOW redlines from procurement, and the export questionnaire answers. Copy the Deal Desk case ID in all replies.

-Rishi
VP, Sales Operations
From: Tom Hale <t.hale@avalon-thera.com>

Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 15:27:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Avalon Therapeutics - pilot request (need clearance + pricing exception)

Hi Lauren / team — thanks for the quick responses. A few clarifications from our side:
- Data scope: we will provide de-identified variant call files (VCFs) and limited clinical metadata. No raw sequence files will be shared. Human subjects, consented under our IRB; we can provide redacted consent language.
- German subcontractor (HelixLab GmbH) only performs aggregated downstream analytics and will not receive raw VCFs; we can add contractual flow-down language if needed.
- UBO: attached is our signed UBO declaration (Avalon_UBO_statement.pdf).
- Pricing: procurement is pushing for a one-time pilot fee with a 30% discount to keep the pilot within budget. If we can’t get 30%, please propose an alternative (e.g., milestone credits).

Procurement timeline: 12/10 signature target but flexible if security/compliance needs more time. Happy to execute an NDA addendum or data processing addendum to restrict processing to us-east-1.

Best,
Tom Hale

Avalon Therapeutics

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Avalon Therapeutics - pilot request (need clearance + pricing exception)

Thanks for the materials — reviewed the UBO and the questionnaire. Quick conclusions:
1) No sanctions hits in the UBO screening; the German subcontractor does not change the primary export control posture because only aggregated results are shared, but we need a contractual flow-down clause and an attestation that HelixLab will never receive sequence-level data.
2) Conditional: we can approve eligibility for a limited research pilot provided the contract includes (a) processing limited to us-east-1, (b) a data-processing addendum that masks allele-level coverage above a threshold and prohibits reconstruction of raw reads, and (c) quarterly attestations during the pilot that no off-shore transfers of raw data occurred.
3) Pricing: I support Rishi’s conditional approach. Given the commercial sensitivity and the reference potential, I would greenlight up to 25% pilot discount now with the option for an additional 5% post-pilot reference credit if security conditions and contractual flow-down are satisfied.

Please update the Deal Desk case with the conditional clearance language and Marissa can shepherd the memo to Rishi for final approval.

Vivek
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
